findings.evidence: line 150-151: `derivWithin ... = S.generator ⟨S.realOperator t x, ...⟩` for `realOperator_derivWithin_generator`; line 158-161: `derivWithin ... = S.realOperator t (S.generator ...)` for bare `realOperator_derivWithin`; line 104-105 bare hasDerivWithinAt uses generator form; line 57-58 bare derivWithin_zero uses generator form.
findings.fix: Swap the derivWithin pair to match: make bare `realOperator_derivWithin` the generator form `A (S t x)` (consistent with hasDerivWithinAt and the `_zero` lemmas) and rename the map-form variant to `realOperator_derivWithin_map_generator` (mirroring `realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_map_generator`).
findings.issue: Bare `realOperator_derivWithin` states the map form `S t (A x)`, but bare `realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt` (line 102) and bare `realOperator_derivWithin_zero` (line 55) both state the generator form `A (S t x)`. So `realOperator_derivWithin` and `realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt` share a base name yet carry different derivatives, and `realOperator_derivWithin` contradicts its own zero-time counterpart.

summary: The two nonnegative-time derivWithin lemmas invert the suffix scheme used by the hasDerivWithinAt pair and by the merged zero-time lemmas: the bare realOperator_derivWithin states the map form S t (A x) while bare realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt and bare realOperator_derivWithin_zero state the generator form A (S t x). Same base name, different derivative, breaking consistency.
